subject: How to decide priors for Bym2

messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: How to decide priors for Bym2
parts:
I'm confused on setting priors for bym2. I know how code it, but I don't have a good intuition on what the numbers mean. However, when I plot a map based on a model with default bym2 priors it tends to look speckled, which I think might imply my priors are not properly calibrated for the iid vs besag elements of my model.

My model specified like so:
formula.allcases.bym2 = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym2", graph="nb.sa.txt")
mod.allcases <- inla(formula.allcases.bym2, data=as.data.frame(SA), family="poisson", E = exTOT,
                         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1, cdf=c(0)),
                         control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, config = TRUE), verbose=TRUE, num.threads = 10,
                     control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd") )


The map of RR's tends to look speckled as I said (small section but its throughout the map):














And a plot of the hyperparameters with priors shown looks like this:















I've tried changing the pc prior:
formula.allcases.bym2 = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym2", graph="nb.sa.txt",
                                      hyper = list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.001))))
but it made little difference. 
I know that prior = "pc" is the mixing parameter phi with default (0.5, 0.5), but I don''t know in what way i should change it. In particular how do I need to change both 0.5's or just one ?
thanks for any advice!

Many thanks for the link, I've just gone thru it as best I could but its very abstract for me, I can't relate it to my question about speckling in the maps above.

The mixing parameter goes from 0 to 1 with 0 being maximally unstructured, and 1 being maximally structured. This i get, but I'm unclear what is the form of the distribution for phi - is it a beta distribution? I can't find that specified anywhere.

Thanks, James
